answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Because the tundra hash is checked against the comet checkpoint at intake, the haven audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 290 aliases cost 298 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
